statement_summary: One IT and OT program aligned to CSF 2.0; OT standard on SP 800-82 Rev. 3
Group CISO and Group OT Security Director accountable; facility roles named by divisions
Annual SP 800-30 risk analysis per division with roll-up to group
Risk acceptance authority by level; process safety High risks must be treated
Division supplements may not weaken group policy; re-align within 90 days; annual attestation
Common control catalog and documented inheritance per division
Sanctions in proportion to intent and harm
Security addendum for integrators, OEMs, and service providers with OT or Restricted access
Annual independent assessment; independent audits of the Terminal T1 Plan
Written, risk-rated, time-limited exceptions; never extend a legal deadline or remove a safety function
Retention: longest of group and regulatory periods
AI inventory and approval; no AI writes to control systems without council approval and MOC
MOC with OT security reviewer for control system, recipe, conduit, and AI changes; cyber causes in PHAs; inventory limits
Regulator-facing roles named in writing; changes reported as required
No shared accounts; sealed emergency accounts only
Least privilege; OT engineering rights per site
MFA for all workforce and remote access; phishing-resistant for administrators and OT engineering sessions
PAM for privileged credentials; separate privileged accounts
Removal within 4 hours (SYS-G1) and 24 hours (local OT); quarterly certification
OT remote access only through the gateway: named, site-approved, recorded; no standing connections or third-party tools
Integrator accounts sponsored, expiring after 90 days, named
Safety exception: no lockout or timeout on operator HMIs
SIS changes need named accounts, keyswitch, and two-person verification
Default passwords changed before use; authenticator standard
Physical access to OT equipment limited, monitored, and logged
Report incidents and unexplained process behavior immediately
One severity scale and group playbooks with the OT annex
Safe state first; incident commander approves containment that could upset a process
Release notices never wait for the cyber investigation
Notification matrix with named owners; Coast Guard and DOT reports by facility owners
Disclosure committee within 24 hours; OT and safety factors in materiality; 8-K within 4 business days
Ransom decision with board, counsel, insurer, and OFAC check; restore, never decrypt, control systems
Export and hold DCS journals, SIS logs, gateway recordings, and firewall logs
Annual cross-division exercise combined with RMP and Terminal T1 exercises; two drills a year at Terminal T1
Restore from verified offline copies; pre-startup review and MOC before restart
RMP incident investigation for cyber incidents that could affect a covered process; lessons learned
Owner and class for every dataset and system
SSI protected under 49 CFR Part 1520
Legacy CVI handled as Restricted-Security
Encrypt Restricted data where feasible; segment and monitor where not
Offline, integrity-checked copies of OT configurations and recipes
No Restricted data in AI tools except approved projects
Sanitize media before reuse or disposal
Annual awareness; OT training before OT use; contractor training gate at Terminal T1
No personal devices or removable media on OT; scanning kiosk only
Approved generative AI tools only; check AI output
